title: Design doc for checkpoint bundle v2
acceptance: `docs/DESIGN-v2.md` exists and has sections for: bundle layout, each bundle file's schema, events.jsonl, save_checkpoint input (new structured fields and which old fields stay accepted), save-time checks with their exact error messages, next-action rule, brief layout, carry-forward by task id, old-format compatibility, eval changes, out of scope

The layout section names every path in the request: `~/.ai-checkpoint/chats/<chat>/checkpoints/cp-NNN/` with manifest.json, plan.json, decisions.jsonl, facts.jsonl, workspace.json, user_turns.jsonl, verbatim/, open_questions.json, brief.md, and `chats/<chat>/events.jsonl`

The doc states how `<chat>` is turned into a folder name (chat names that differ only in case, contain spaces or non-ASCII) and that cp-NNN ids are global and sequential across chats and old flat files
The doc states the next-action rule as: first task in `order` whose status is todo and whose `depends_on` are all done; and what happens when none qualifies
Out-of-scope list includes SQLite index/ask_checkpoint, embeddings, MCP sampling, online backends; `git diff --stat` for this feature touches only docs/

title: Bundle storage with manifest, events log and old-format compatibility
acceptance: A save through `GitStore(tmp).save(...)` with today's (old-style) fields creates `chats/<chat>/checkpoints/cp-001/` containing manifest.json, plan.json, decisions.jsonl, facts.jsonl, workspace.json, user_turns.jsonl, verbatim/, open_questions.json and brief.md, and makes exactly one new git commit containing only that folder, the chat's events.jsonl and, on the chat's first save only, the chat's chat.json
manifest.json holds id, resumed_from (or null), created_at, client, and a sha256 for every other file in the bundle; recomputing sha256 of each file matches the manifest

Each verbatim item is written as a real file under verbatim/ whose bytes equal the saved text exactly (test with tabs, trailing spaces, CRLF, backticks and non-ASCII); two items with the same label do not overwrite each other
`chats/<chat>/events.jsonl` gains exactly one appended line per save (earlier lines unchanged byte for byte) naming the checkpoint id and event type

With an existing old flat `checkpoints/cp-003.json` in the store, the next save gets id cp-004; `get`, `list`, `resolve` (by id, name, chat/name) and renumbering ('name (1)') work across a mix of old flat files and bundles

Golden test: loading tests/fixtures/old_format_cp.json from a store and calling resume_checkpoint returns text byte-identical to tests/fixtures/old_format_brief.golden.md; old files are never rewritten or moved (file hash unchanged after further saves)

Secrets in any field (e.g. `sk-...` key, `password=...`, bearer token, URL credentials) do not appear in any bundle file, events.jsonl, or the commit message (grep of the store's working tree and `git log -p` finds none)
If git commit fails, the new bundle folder is removed and events.jsonl is unchanged; a corrupt bundle (bad JSON in plan.json) is skipped by list without crashing
`$HOME/aic-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` passes with at least the previous 308 tests (existing tests updated only where the on-disk path is asserted)

title: Structured plan, computed next action, v2 brief and save echo
acceptance: save_checkpoint (MCP tool and GitStore.save) accepts new optional fields: tasks (text, status todo|in_progress|done, from user|ai, quote, depends_on, order), decisions with status/supersedes, facts (key, value, valid_from, superseded_by), user_turns, open_questions with waiting_on_user; a call with only the old fields still succeeds
The server assigns task ids (t-1, t-2, ... in order) and writes them to plan.json; client-supplied ids on a fresh plan are ignored or rejected as documented

Next action = first task by order with status todo whose depends_on are all done; test: t-1 done, t-2 todo depends_on [t-3], t-3 todo -> next action is t-3; an in_progress task is preferred if the design says so, and this is tested
depends_on naming an unknown task or forming a cycle returns a clear validation error and writes nothing
brief.md (and resume_checkpoint output) opens with a 'Next action' section naming the computed task, followed by the user's own plan (from=user tasks with their quotes) before AI tasks
Brief includes a 'No longer needed' section listing workspace items with status done_with; the section is omitted when there are none
When only old fields are given, next_steps become tasks (lines starting "User's plan:" become from=user) so the brief still opens with 'Next action'
The save result includes the text `Next action saved: <task text>. Correct?` with the computed task
brief.md is regenerated from the other files: deleting brief.md and calling resume returns the same text

title: Save-time code checks returned as fixable errors
acceptance: A from=user task whose quote does not match any user_turns entry or last_exchange.user (matching is case-, whitespace- and punctuation-insensitive per decisions.md ruling 2) is rejected; the error names the task and the quote, and nothing is written (no folder, no commit, no events line)
Matching tolerates case, whitespace and punctuation differences but not different words: a test pins one accepted variant (e.g. extra spaces/capitals) and one rejected variant (a changed word)
A plan whose tasks are all done (or empty) is rejected with an error saying at least one unfinished task is needed

No free-text heuristic check on decision reasons (dropped in the F-001 amendment): a decision with empty rejected is accepted; checks apply only to decisions and tasks that are new or changed in this save, never to items carried forward unchanged from the parent (test with a parent whose decision has empty rejected)
All failing checks are reported together in one error (not first-only), and the MCP tool returns them as an error result the chat model can read
A valid save passes all checks; old-field-only saves are not rejected by checks that need new fields (documented which checks apply)
Secrets in quotes/user_turns are redacted before the verbatim-quote check, and the check does not fail merely because redaction changed both sides equally

title: Carry-forward plan updates by task id from a resumed chat
acceptance: The brief of a bundle checkpoint shows each task's id (e.g. `[t-2]`)

save with resumed_from=cp-001 and plan_updates [{id: t-2, status: done}, {text: 'new task', from: ai}] produces a plan.json that keeps all parent tasks (ids, quotes, order) with t-2 done and a new task with the next unused id
An update naming an unknown task id returns a validation error naming the id; nothing is written
Unmentioned parent decisions, facts, workspace and user_turns are carried forward unless replaced; the events.jsonl line records resumed_from
plan_updates without resumed_from returns a clear error; resumed_from pointing at an old flat checkpoint converts its next_steps into tasks first, then applies updates
The computed next action and the save echo reflect the updated plan

title: Eval support for the bundle path (offline)
acceptance: compaction_system_prompt() describes the new structured fields from the same schema source as the MCP tool (a test asserts the tool's field descriptions appear in the prompt)
The eval checkpoint handover builds the brief through the bundle path (store save into a temp dir, then resume), and records save-check errors in the result instead of aborting
FakeModel's compaction output uses the new fields (tasks with from=user quotes taken verbatim from the transcript, user_turns, workspace with done_with items) and passes the save checks

`checkpoint-eval suite datasets/handover-v2/*.json --model fake --out <tmp>` completes offline with no API key and no network, writing results.json and results.md for all 6 scenarios with a checkpoint handover for each
Old-format path stays available (flag or mode) so previous runs can be reproduced; existing eval tests pass
eval-runs/README.md documents how to run v2 for real; the real-model target (next step >=90%, key-fact recall >=88%) is recorded as a separate manual run, not an offline test
